name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Bill Keating holds a roughly ten-to-one cash advantage in a D+6 Massachusetts district
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 96%
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so fundamentals carry the outlook
Challenger Tyler MacAllister has raised modestly and has little cash on hand
model.rationale: Fundamentals point firmly to Keating: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a large financial edge, with markets pricing a near-certain hold and no polling suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending for MacAllister or a sharp shift in the national environment could narrow the margin, though no current signal points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 9th District leans Democratic by six points on partisanship, and incumbent Bill Keating returns with the advantages of a tenured House member. He has raised about $535,000 and holds more than $511,000 on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has raised roughly $213,000 with about $52,000 available. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and market pricing.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side near 96 percent, consistent with a comfortable hold. Massachusetts Republicans have struggled in federal races even in favorable years, and the challenger lacks the resources to change the dynamic quickly. The expected margin is roughly eighteen points, with the seat rated Safe Democratic and moderate confidence given the absence of direct polling in the district.
